summary: Independent GRAVEYARD adversarial pass challenged all 12 Chief-selected active-batch companies for concentration, regulation, capital intensity, dilution, cyclicality, execution and substitution risk. No company is falsified outright, but several have material hidden fragilities that must remain visible before methodology-1.0 promotion. The common macro failure mode is correlated hyperscaler/AI-capex dependence across a batch that can otherwise look diversified by ticker.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Record $2.36B backlog can hide execution duration, cancellation rights and margin mix; launch/space-systems integration plus Neutron capex create schedule and capital-allocation risk even with >$2B liquidity reported earlier in 2026.
contradictions: Rapid revenue/backlog growth is real, but it does not prove Neutron economics or backlog conversion quality.
unknowns: Current contractual cancellation/termination composition of backlog and exact Neutron cash requirement.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Repeated schedule slips, material backlog cancellations, or sustained negative unit economics despite scale.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Customer concentration is extreme: top 10 ~90% of FY2026 revenue, with end-customer profiles B/D/E at 32%/33%/19%. This is the clearest batch-level fragility and can create cliff risk if one hyperscaler changes architecture or procurement.
contradictions: Explosive revenue growth and 68% gross margin coexist with unusually concentrated demand.
unknowns: Duration and pricing protections of top hyperscaler programs; how much reported diversification is contracting-entity versus true end-customer diversification.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A top customer program loss or mix shift causes abrupt growth/margin compression.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Scorpio becoming the largest product family introduces product-ramp concentration and execution risk. Inventory increased sharply into the ramp, and high growth can obscure dependence on a narrow set of AI platform programs.
contradictions: Q2 profitability and >70% gross margins reduce solvency risk, but do not remove design-win concentration or product-transition risk.
unknowns: Exact end-customer revenue concentration for Q2 and cancellation visibility on Scorpio-related demand.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Scorpio ramp underperforms guidance or a major platform design is delayed/lost.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: NVIDIA's filing explicitly shows concentrated direct/indirect customers and severe China-policy exposure. H20/H200 restrictions created billions in charges and current H200 China shipments remain tiny; geopolitical exclusion can accelerate domestic Chinese alternatives and customer diversification away from NVIDIA.
contradictions: Exceptional demand and platform strength coexist with policy-created addressable-market loss and high customer concentration.
unknowns: Long-run effect of custom accelerators on hyperscaler wallet share and whether sovereign restrictions broaden beyond current geographies/products.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Major CSPs materially reduce external GPU share while gross margin compresses and software moat weakens.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Data Center growth is strong, but accelerator success depends on catching a dominant incumbent while export controls can remove China demand. MI308/MI325 licensing creates inventory, tariff and competitive uncertainty; software ecosystem execution remains critical.
contradictions: Q2 Data Center revenue nearly doubled YoY, but growth alone does not prove durable accelerator share or superior economics.
unknowns: Instinct customer concentration, normalized accelerator gross margin and repeat-order breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: MI-series demand remains concentrated/pilot-sized or software/ecosystem gaps prevent repeat scaling.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: AI acceleration is extraordinary but potentially concentrated in a small number of custom-accelerator customers and financed megaprojects. VMware integration adds software execution/debt history; custom silicon economics can be powerful but customer bargaining power is also unusually high.
contradictions: 46% FCF margin in Q3 is a major buffer, yet concentration and project-finance dependence can still create nonlinear downside.
unknowns: Customer-level AI revenue shares, project cancellation protections, and exact debt reduction path after VMware.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: One or more hyperscaler custom programs migrate away or financed capacity projects materially delay.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: TSMC is a technological bottleneck but also a geopolitical single point of failure. Overseas fabs reduce but do not eliminate Taiwan concentration; leading-edge capex is enormous and duplicated geographic capacity can structurally raise cost.
contradictions: 534 customers and broad end markets diversify commercial demand while physical production concentration remains high.
unknowns: Fully normalized overseas-fab margin dilution and customer willingness to pay geographic-resilience premiums.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A durable process/yield lead by a competitor or a Taiwan disruption materially impairs advanced-node output.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: EUV monopoly-like positioning is exposed to export controls and customer capex concentration. Record backlog can unwind if memory/foundry customers delay fab ramps; High-NA adoption also risks slower productivity/economic payback than technical capability suggests.
contradictions: Backlog and 50%+ gross margins signal pricing power, but policy and customer-capex cyclicality remain outside ASML's control.
unknowns: Current 2026 China sales mix and High-NA utilization economics at leading customers.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: High-NA ROI disappoints and major customers materially defer tool orders while export restrictions broaden.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top five customers are ~57% of revenue; Arm China ~16%, and SoftBank-linked arrangements add related-party/strategic dependence. RISC-V and customer-owned designs are credible long-horizon substitution vectors.
contradictions: Near-98% gross margins and royalty growth show strong economics, but concentrated ecosystem dependence can make apparent asset-light resilience less robust than it looks.
unknowns: Incremental royalty economics in data center versus mobile and long-run RISC-V share capture.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Key hyperscalers/licensees shift substantial new silicon to RISC-V or proprietary ISA without compensating Arm royalty growth.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: The record quarter is so far above prior-cycle memory economics that mean-reversion risk is central. HBM scarcity and long-term agreements can stabilize demand, but industry capex expansion can eventually destroy pricing power; heavy capex remains unavoidable.
contradictions: Strategic customer agreements improve visibility while the underlying memory industry remains cyclical and supply-responsive.
unknowns: Contract floors/take-or-pay details and competitor HBM4 yield/capacity trajectories.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: HBM share/yield deteriorates or industry supply growth causes rapid ASP/gross-margin normalization.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Exceptional margins and AI-networking growth can hide concentration in a few cloud titans. Ethernet is gaining AI relevance, but hyperscalers can use internal software/hardware or alternate fabrics; inventory and deferred revenue expansion should be watched for demand timing effects.
contradictions: Large cash/securities balance reduces financing risk while customer/architecture concentration remains strategic rather than financial.
unknowns: Current top-two customer share and attach rate of new 1.6T platforms across multiple independent buyers.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Cloud-titan spend decelerates sharply or proprietary/alternative fabrics take material scale-out share.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: A 2.9x book-to-bill and 109% backlog growth can reflect genuine scarcity, but it also creates cancellation/double-ordering and execution risk. Vertiv must convert a very large backlog while navigating tariffs, component constraints and customer data-center power availability.
contradictions: Broad-based order growth supports demand durability, yet hyperscale/colocation remains the primary driver of the surge.
unknowns: Backlog cancellation terms, aging profile and current customer concentration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog conversion slows materially, cancellations rise, or power/interconnection delays push customer projects out multiple years.

materialFindings.finding: CRDO has the sharpest directly quantified customer-concentration risk in the batch: top-10 ~90% and three end customers represented 32%, 33% and 19% of FY2026 revenue.
NVDA and AMD both retain material export-control exposure; the same policy regime can simultaneously impair revenue and strengthen local substitutes, a second-order competitive effect.
ARM combines customer concentration with Arm China and SoftBank-linked dependencies; this must not be hidden by asset-light gross margins.

The batch is structurally correlated to the same AI-capex regime. A broad hyperscaler capex reset could hit NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, ALAB, TSM, ASML, MU, ANET and VRT together, making ticker count a poor proxy for thesis diversification.

contradictions: Record backlog/orders across RKLB and VRT improve demand visibility but do not establish cancellation quality, margins or schedule credibility.
Record AI revenue across multiple semiconductor/interconnect names is partly common-origin hyperscaler spending and should not be interpreted as fully independent corroboration.
unknowns: Normalized current valuation is outside this lane and remains for expectations-execution.
Several companies still lack exact current customer-concentration disclosures normalized on a comparable end-customer basis.
Contractual cancellation rights and backlog aging are not consistently disclosed across the batch.

peerRequests.request: Prioritize CRDO/ALAB/ANET customer-concentration normalization and RKLB/VRT backlog quality before promotion.
Model one correlated AI-capex downshift as a common shock across the semiconductor/interconnect/power-cooling cluster.
Penalize opportunity confidence where record growth/backlog requires aggressive continuation assumptions or current valuation cannot be sourced reproducibly.

accuracyDebates.reason: The active batch is nominally 12 companies but economically concentrated in one AI-infrastructure spending regime.
Backlog/book-to-bill without cancellation/aging terms can overstate durable demand for RKLB and VRT.
